officialDocs.label: List your app in the Gong Collective
What the Gong API provides (rate limits)

verdict.summary: You can build and test an OAuth app in a Gong developer instance (which takes up to five working days to get), but the app stays Private, usable only in your own account, until you publish it in the Gong Collective. Gong describes that as a process for partners: you submit a Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form and must register trusted IP addresses. Once installed, a Gong tech admin has to approve the scopes for the whole company.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: 'This can take up to five working days' for the developer instance; creating the integration itself takes under an hour. A tech admin at an existing Gong customer could create a private app in their own instance sooner.

timeToProd.assumes: A published Gong Collective OAuth app reading calls and transcripts (api:calls:read:transcript etc.) that any Gong customer's tech admin can install.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Gong partner review after the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form (Gong says it contacts you within five business days to finalize the release), plus Collective listing setup.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Only the five-day developer instance and the five-day first-contact figures are published. The full range is our estimate.

verdict.cost: No developer fee is documented. Your end users need paid Gong seats, and available API features depend on their plan.

Publishing to the Gong Collective is described as a process for Partners and goes through a Technology Partner review form.

prerequisites.why: These are required fields when registering the integration.

scopeTiers.impact: The only scopes that support Personal access (per-user) instead of Shared access. The authorization context can't be changed after setup, so decide up front.
Upload calls, push CRM data, manage tasks and flows, or delete data. Changing scopes after publication requires a support ticket.

steps.title: Request a developer instance
steps.detail: Fill in Gong's form for a developer instance (linked from step 1 of the guide). You get login credentials when it's ready.

steps.title: Wait for the developer instance
steps.detail: Gong says this can take up to five working days.

steps.title: Pick scopes and authorization context
steps.detail: Map the agent's endpoints to scopes using the API reference. Choose Shared or Personal access; it can't be edited later, and Personal only works with AI and MCP scopes.

steps.title: Draft listing content and policies
steps.detail: Write the name, short and long descriptions, help article, privacy policy and terms (covering AI processing of call data), and the authorization start page copy.

steps.title: Create the integration
steps.detail: Admin center > Settings > Ecosystem card > API > Integrations tab > CREATE INTEGRATION. Fill in fields, logos, scopes, redirect URI, contacts and allowed IPs; copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect a tech admin to https://app.gong.io/oauth2/authorize; exchange the code (valid 10 min) at POST https://app.gong.io/oauth2/generate-customer-token with Basic auth; store api_base_url_for_customer per customer and refresh with grant_type=refresh_token.

steps.title: Test in the sandbox
steps.detail: Authorize the private app in your developer instance and confirm calls, transcripts and 429 handling work.

steps.title: Submit the partner review form
steps.detail: Submit the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form on the Gong Collective site, with trusted IPs configured.

steps.title: Wait for Gong to finalize release
steps.detail: Gong contacts you within five business days to finalize the release and Collective listing. The full review length isn't stated.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Five business days to first contact is sourced; the rest is our estimate.

blockers.symptom: Other Gong customers can't install your app
blockers.cause: New apps are Private and usable only in your own Gong account until published to the Gong Collective.
blockers.fix: Submit the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form and publish.

blockers.cause: No trusted IP addresses are configured for the integration.
blockers.fix: Add your static egress IPs (e.g. via a NAT gateway or proxy if you're on serverless).

blockers.symptom: API calls fail for a customer after a successful token exchange
blockers.cause: Requests went to a generic host instead of the customer's api_base_url_for_customer.
blockers.fix: Save api_base_url_for_customer per customer and send all API calls there.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The symptom is inferred; the per-customer URL requirement is sourced.

blockers.cause: A tech admin has to sign in and approve the scopes for shared-access apps.
blockers.fix: Ask customers to have a Gong tech admin run the install, or use Personal access for AI/MCP-only scopes.

blockers.cause: Default limits are 3 calls per second and 10,000 per day.
blockers.fix: Honour Retry-After, spread backfills over days, or ask Gong for higher limits.

blockers.symptom: Need a new scope after publication
blockers.cause: Scope changes on a published OAuth app go through Gong support.
blockers.fix: Open a support ticket, then have customers re-authorize.

nuances.text: Access tokens are valid for 1 day by default and can be changed with validity_duration; refreshing returns a new refresh token. The docs' example shows expires_in 525600, which doesn't match the 1-day default.
Each customer has its own API host (e.g. https://company-17.api.gong.io), returned as api_base_url_for_customer.
Rate limits default to 3 calls/sec and 10,000 calls/day, with 429 and Retry-After when exceeded.
Shared access is company-wide: one tech admin's approval exposes all calls the scopes cover. Per-user Personal access is limited to ai-ask, ai-briefer and MCP scopes.
For a single company, an API access key from the tech admin is an alternative to OAuth; the help center links to Manage API keys.
